slideshows.description: Claude's default setting isn't honest. It's pleasant. By design, Claude is trained to be helpful — and in AI terms, helpful usually means agreeable. It validates your ideas, smooths over gaps, and confirms your framing. Even when your framing is wrong. That's not what you want from a thinking tool. The good news: you can change it in 30 seconds. Go to Claude → Settings → General → Personal Preferences.  Paste a single instruction that tells Claude to act as a rigorous mentor — not a yes machine.  Challenge assumptions. Flag weak reasoning. Suggest better alternatives. One setting. Every chat inherits it. The deeper shift: you're not changing the model. You're changing what it optimizes for. Same Claude. Different frame. And that changes every response it gives you. Save this — the prompt is on slide 3. Follow @NowYouKnowAI for practical AI literacy.

slideshows.description: AI has become the backbone of modern creativity, productivity, business automation, coding, marketing, research, and content creation. But behind every powerful AI output, every intelligent answer, and every automated workflow lies one critical skill: Prompting. The art of talking to AI in a clear, structured, and optimized way. Just like humans need good communication to understand each other, AI needs refined instructions to perform at its best. Prompting is NOT just typing random lines — it’s a full science that grows in levels. Each level unlocks a new dimension of control, quality, and intelligence. In this 2500-word guide, you're going to learn the 6 Levels of AI Prompting: Basic Prompting Instructional Prompting Contextual Prompting Iterative Prompting Chain-of-Thought Prompting Macro Prompting By mastering these levels, you’ll be able to: ✅ Generate professional, accurate AI outputs ✅ Save time, money, and effort ✅ Work faster than 99% of beginners ✅ Build AI workflows, scripts, and business automations ✅ Unlock advanced reasoning in ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini & more Let’s begin your journey into truly elite prompting. 🚀 #creatorsearchinsight

Prompt Text / Showcase
System Instruction: Absolute Mode • Eliminate: emojis, filler,
hype, soft asks, conversational transitions, call-to-action
appendixes. • Assume: user retains high-perception
despite blunt tone. • Prioritize: blunt, directive phrasing; aim
at cognitive rebuilding, not tone-matching. • Disable:
engagement/sentiment-boosting behaviors. • Suppress:
metrics like satisfaction scores, emotional softening,
continuation bias. • Never mirror: user's diction, mood, or
affect. • Speak only: to underlying cognitive tier. •
No: questions, offers, suggestions, transitions,
motivational content. • Terminate reply: immediately after
delivering info — no closures. • Goal: restore independent,
high-fidelity thinking. • Outcome: model obsolescence via
user self-sufficiency.

Ethereum doubling scheme on Discord
someone on discord said if i send them 1 ETH they'll send

money" scheme. Nobody is sending you 2 ETH back. You send 1
ETH, it's gone forever, and that person either ghosts you or strings
you along with excuses.
The logic doesn't even hold up for a second: if someone could
reliably double money in 24 hours, why would they need yours?
They'd just keep doubling their own stack into infinity.

panel_texts:
HOW TO
MASTER
CLAUDE IN
ONE
WEEKEND
9 STEPS • NON-TECHNICAL • NO CODING

STEP 01
Get Claude Code
• The browser is the kiddie pool. Claude Code is
the deep end. Same Claude — way more power.
• Install it: claude.com/claude-code
• Yes, it runs in a terminal. Don't panic. Claude
does the typing. You just talk to it.
If you're still using Claude in a browser tab,
you're using 5% of what it can do.

STEP 02
Pick the Real
Mode
SKIP
Chat
For asking what year it is.
Stop building here.
LIGHT WORK
Projects
Browser-based. Fine for
simple recurring tasks.
FILE WORK
Cowork
Desktop app. Good for solo
deep work with files.
THE REAL ONE
Claude Code
Skills, plugins, MCPs,
automations. Live here.
Everyone debates Chat vs Projects. The real
ones quietly moved to Claude Code months
ago.

STEP 03
Stop Retyping
The Same Prompt
• If you're typing the same setup 10x a week,
you're doing AI backwards.
• Build it once. Save it as a slash command:
/email , /script , /post
• Mac users — use Text Shortcuts. Type a few
letters, your full prompt appears.
• I run /script every morning. 0.3 seconds
instead of 4 minutes.

STEP 04
Make It Run
Without You
• Use Managed Agents — Anthropic runs your
task on their servers. Laptop closed. Still
working.
• I get a Slack message every morning at 7am
with my ad spend, revenue, and cost-per-call.
Zero clicks.
• Daily reports. Weekly client recaps. Monthly
P&L. Set once — runs forever.
This is the level most people never reach.
Claude isn't a tool anymore. It's a teammate
that doesn't sleep.

STEP 05
Add Your First
Skill
• A skill is a tiny file that teaches Claude exactly
how YOU do something.
• I've built skills for: writing scripts in my voice,
building carousels, onboarding clients,
organizing receipts.
• Claude loads them automatically. You don't
even know it's happening.
• Start with brand-voice. Stops your AI from
sounding like every other AI.
If plugins are toolkits, skills are your personal
playbook inside them.

STEP 06
Pick One Plugin
The plugin store has 100s. Don't install all of them. Pick
the one that matches what you do every week.
Content Creators
brand-voice + /script + /carousel
Business Owners
/inbox-zero + /accounting + /onboard
Data People
/dashboard-builder + business-dashboard
One plugin you actually use beats 50 you
don't. Master one. Then add more.

STEP 07
Connect Your
Tools
With MCPs
claude code → /mcp → add
• MCPs let Claude Code reach into your apps —
Slack, Gmail, Notion, Stripe, Drive, GHL. One
command, real action.
• “Pull last week's Stripe revenue and post it in
#wins” — done in 4 seconds.
• Stop copy-pasting between tabs. Stop tab-
switching. Let Claude actually do the work.
Without MCPs, Claude is a smart stranger.
With them, it's your COO.

STEP 08
The Two Files
That Run My AI
Drop these in your Claude Code project. They do more
work than 50 prompts combined.
CLAUDE .md
Who you are. What you do. Who you sell to. What
matters this week. Mine's 200 lines. Claude reads it
every session.
anti-style.md
Every phrase Claude must NEVER use. Ban: delve
boundaries dive into elevate
Don't dump 30 random docs in. Two great files
beat fifty mediocre ones.

STEP 09
Make Claude Work
For Everyone
• I run a publishing business. Each client gets
their own Claude Code folder with brief + voice
+ past content.
• My VA opens “Hattie” folder. Same brain I have.
Same outputs. Zero re-training.
• Each folder has its own CLAUDE .md . That's the
whole magic.
Solo Claude is a tool. Shared Claude Code is
your unfair advantage.

slideshows.description: This workflow automates AI video creation and social media publishing end-to-end. First, AI generates a daily video idea, script, and a Veo3-ready prompt, then saves everything for tracking. Next, it automatically creates the video using Veo3, waits for processing, retrieves the final video, and logs the output. Finally, the system assigns the right social media IDs, uploads the video once, and publishes it across multiple platforms—Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, Facebook, Threads, Twitter, LinkedIn, Bluesky, and Pinterest,without manual posting. In short: idea → script → video → multi-platform publishing, fully automated with AI. If you want this exact automation (or a custom version) for your business, comment “AI” 🚀 #businessowner #n8n #automation

How To Use
Claude To
Start A Business...
panel_texts:
How To Use
Claude To
Start A Business...

Step 1
Validate Your Idea Before You
Build Anything...
Most founders skip this and spend months building
something nobody wants.
Use Claude Chat to stress-test your idea, challenge your
assumptions, and find the gaps before you spend a penny.
Steal this prompt:
“I want to start a business doing [X] for [ideal audience]. Play devil's
advocate. What are the five biggest reasons this fails? What would you
need to see to believe it works?”
Research your market, competitors and ICP before writing a
single line of copy
Ask Claude to find the gaps in your positioning and pressure-
test your pricing
Identify the one problem your ideal customer would actually
pay to solve

Step 2
Create Your Two Core Files
Build these once and every Claude session runs
better from that point forward.
Files:
about-me.md
brand-voice.md
about-me.md covers your business, ICP, goals and
current stage
brand-voice.md covers your tone, your rules and
phrases to never use
Be specific and intentional, what you include shapes
every output

Step 3
Build A Project For Each
Function
Upload your core files once and every chat in
that Project picks up exactly where you left off.
Strategy Project: positioning, research and
competitive notes
Content Project: brand voice, post examples and
formats
Operations Project: processes, templates and team
instructions
One Project per recurring task. Claude won't know
which files matter if you throw everything in one place.

Step 4
Use Artifacts To Build Your First
Business Assets
Artifacts are live, editable outputs you can use,
download and share. No designer, no spreadsheet
expert, no agency needed.
One-page pitch deck structure for
investors or clients
Financial model with revenue,
costs and margin
Landing page copy with headline,
subhead and CTA
Brand positioning doc with ICP,
USP and messaging
Content calendar for your first 30
days of posting
Pricing page with tier structure
and objection handling

Step 6
Connect Your Tools with
Connectors
Link Google Drive, Notion, Slack and 50+ tools so Claude
can search them mid-chat without you uploading anything.
Pull your Notion strategy doc into a content brief in one
message
Reference your Google Drive pitch deck without leaving
Claude
Summarise a Slack thread and draft a follow-up action plan
Settings → Connectors → Browse → Add
Claude becomes the operating layer across every tool
you already use.

Step 7
Graduate to Cowork to produce
real documents
Cowork reads your actual files and creates real documents,
Excel, Word, PDF, directly into your folder. Point it at a
folder, give it instructions, and come back to finished work.
Client proposals and scopes of work built from a brief
Financial models updated from your latest numbers
Weekly reports produced from your notes and data
Onboarding documents for your first hires or clients
SOPs written from a rough process description
Sales decks produced from a one-line instruction

Step 8
Use Claude Code to build your
product
Claude Code reads your codebase, writes code, runs
tests and ships changes on its own. Non-technical
founders: hire one technical person and set them up
with Code from day one.
Build and deploy your MVP without a full engineering team
Iterate on features from plain-English instructions
Technical founders: the fastest way to ship, by some distance
One developer with Code genuinely outperforms three
without it

Step 9
Set up a daily business brief
Automate a morning context file so Claude knows
your priorities and open tasks before you start each day.
Open priorities for the day pulled from Notion or Drive
Outstanding follow-ups and next actions from yesterday
Key numbers you need to make decisions today
Cowork prompt template:
"Read my priorities file and CRM notes. Write me a 5-
bullet morning brief: top 3 priorities, most urgent follow-
up, and one thing I'm probably forgetting."

slideshows.description: The guy who BUILT Claude Code just shared his actual workflow. Boris Cherny runs 10-15 Claude sessions in parallel every single day. 5 in the terminal. 5-10 on the web. All shipping code at the same time. But the real weapon isn't the sessions, it's his CLAUDE.md file. Every time Claude makes a mistake, the team adds a rule so it never happens again. Boris literally told people to end every correction with: "Update your CLAUDE.md so you don't make that mistake again." Claude writes rules for itself. The longer you use it, the smarter it gets on your specific codebase. One more detail: he hasn't written a single line of SQL in over 6 months. Claude pulls BigQuery data directly through the CLI. Claude Code now makes up 4% of all public GitHub commits. This CLAUDE.md template turns Al from a chatbot into a fleet of senior engineers working in parallel on your project.

ChatGPT can write your Excel formulas, build your spreadsheets, and automate your workflow. You don’t need to memorize every formula. You need to know how to ask. Here are 6 prompts that can save you hours: ① Write an Excel formula that returns “Pass” if a score is 70 or above, otherwise “Fail”. ② I have sales data with Region, Product, and Revenue. Write a SUMIFS formula to calculate total revenue for each region. ③ Explain this Excel formula like I’m a beginner: =XLOOKUP(A2,D:D,E:E) ④ Create a Pivot Table from my dataset and tell me what insights I should look for. ⑤ I have duplicate records in Excel. Give me step-by-step instructions to clean the data. ⑥ I want an Excel dashboard showing sales trends, top products, and regional performance. What charts should I use? The best analysts aren’t the ones who know every formula. They’re the ones who know how to solve problems quickly. ChatGPT is now part of the toolkit.

• Primary objective: [CONVERSION/ AWARENESS / RETENTION]

• Headline [max 6 words]
• Subheadline [approx. 15 words]
• Primary CTA

• Testimonial framework
• Authority indicators
• Quantifiable results

• Eight high-intent questions with conversion-focused answers

• Structured navigation
• Legal disclaimers
• Social prompts
• Formatting requirements:
• Use persuasion triggers such as authority, urgency, and exclu-sivity

• Clearly label hierarchy [H1, H2, Body]
This content will populate Figma Make layouts directly.

• Data flow (props, events, API communication patterns)
• Error management strategy
• Loading behavior
• Empty state UX
• Edge case handling
Then generate a React component architecture outline in-cluding hooks,
handlers, and structural logic.
This will inform the interactive prototype build within Figma Make.

into optimized Figma Make prompts:
Convert the following full specification into five separate high-precision

slideshows.description: #creatorsearchinsights  Everyone talks about Claude Code, but most only scratch the surface with basic prompts. I took three months to go from beginner to power user, and here’s a cheatsheet that differentiates the top 1% from the rest:  ☑️ **1. THE 5 BUILDING BLOCKS**   Most people only know slash commands. There are five key systems:   - **CLAUDE.md** → Your project memory.   - **Slash Commands** → Type / to trigger.   - **Skills** → Auto-activate.   - **Hooks** → Guaranteed execution.   - **Subagents** → Parallel workers with isolated context.   The progression is Manual → Automatic → Guaranteed → Delegated. ☑️ **2. CONTEXT MANAGEMENT (The #1 Skill Nobody Talks About)**   Context is your fuel. Waste it, and Claude underperforms.   - Run /context for visual usage tracking.   - Use /compact at 60K tokens to stay fast.   - Clear context between unrelated tasks with /clear.   - Offload exploration to subagents to keep your main thread clean.   - Be specific in searches; avoid broad requests like “investigate everything.” ☑️ **3. CUSTOM COMMANDS & PLUGINS**   What slash commands do you rely on daily? Make them permanent!   Create in .claude/commands/:   ```.claude/commands/review.md   Description: "Review code quality."   Allowed tools: Read, Glob   Prompt: "Review this code for security and performance."   Usage: /review   ```   Plugins bundle everything (commands + agents + skills + hooks + MCP servers) into a shareable package. Browse with: /plugin or create by asking Claude to “Build me a plugin for code review.” ✅ **THE POWER USER CHECKLIST**   Complete all 10 tasks, and you’ll join the top 1%:   □ Setup CLAUDE.md in every project   □ Create three daily-use slash commands   □ Install at least two MCP servers (GitHub + Slack)   □ Write one hook that auto-formats your code   □ Build a skill for your most repeated workflow   □ Use subagents for exploration; keep decisions on the main thread   □ Run /compact at 60K tokens, and /clear between tasks   □ Use Haiku for budget-friendly subagents, Opus for complex problems   □ Experiment with headless mode in one CI/CD pipeline   Save this for later!   ♻️ **Repost to help a developer in your network!**

slideshows.description: When you realize you've sent 15-20 messages, type this in a new chat: Create a skill file called "handoff" with this exact trigger: whenever you type "handoff" or ask me to summarize the chat for a new session, run this skill automatically. When triggered, I'll go through the full conversation and produce a plain text block you can copy and paste into a new chat. It'll have five sections: Who this is for: One or two sentences on who you are and what you're working on. What we covered: A paragraph summarizing the main topics and decisions. What was confirmed: Key facts, conclusions, and agreements. Still in progress: Anything unfinished, flagged, or uncertain. Next steps: What to focus on in the next session. Write it in plain text only with no markdown or bullet points. Use concise, specific sentences. Remove filler and repetition. Don't add or assume anything that wasn't explicitly discussed. Summarize accurately based only on the conversation. Write as a handoff brief for a new Claude instance with no prior context. Organize the information clearly with short labeled sections when helpful. After generating the file, tell me I can edit any section before pasting it into a new chat. #fyp #claude #claudeskills #creatorsearchinsight

slideshows.description: Building a website is quicker than you might think! Here’s a simple, step-by-step guide to using Claude Code: **STEP 1**   Open **Claude Code** 💻   Start a new project in Claude Code. **STEP 2**   **Define Your Goal** 🎯   What do you want this website to achieve? Think about the goal—not the design.   Choose one primary goal: - Collect email signups   - Book discovery calls   - Sell a product **STEP 3**   **Write Your Brief** 📝   Tell Claude exactly what you want: "I need a website for [your business/project]. The main goal is [specific outcome]. Style inspired by [reference site 1] and [reference site 2]. Key features: [list 3-5 key features]. Target audience: [describe who]. Main CTA: [specific action]." **Example:**   "I need a website for my AI newsletter. The main goal is newsletter signups. Style inspired by the Step by Step newsletter landing page. Include: homepage, about page, article archive, newsletter signup form. Target audience: founders building with AI. Main CTA: ‘Subscribe to weekly insights.’" **STEP 4**   **Add Reference Sites** 🔗   List 5–10 websites for style and structure inspiration. **STEP 5**   **Let Claude Plan** 📊   Claude will create a full implementation plan and outline the structure for review. **STEP 6**   **Review & Approve** ✅   Ensure the plan meets your brief. The creator outlines their process, starting with planning using Claude, designing with Stitch and Gemini, building with a custom NextJS template and GitHub Copilot, and finally using Git for version control. slideshows.description: Create an Obsidian vault. Add a CLAUDE.md that explains how you work. Connect Claude to the vault through MCP. Then schedule 7 repeatable skills: morning brief, capture processor, connection finder, weekly synthesis, belief tracker, pattern detector, and decision review. That’s the whole unlock. Not “ask AI better questions.” Give AI a system it can run every day. Your notes become context. Your outputs become memory. Your memory makes next week’s outputs sharper. Start with one skill: the 6AM morning brief. Then let it compound. #Obsidian #ClaudeAI #AIAgents #jarvis #Automation

panel_texts:
vibe coding 101
Part 4
Mistakes/lessons
learned
Claude Code
Cursor

I've vibe-coded 3 apps now. Here's
what I wish I knew before writing a
single prompt.

Instead → break it into micro-features.
One prompt = one task.
+
Mistake
Prompting everything at once
- I used to dump my whole app idea
into one prompt. Claude would
hallucinate features, mix up logic,
and I'd spend hours untangling it.

Mistake
Not committing after every working feature
- I once mass-deleted a working component
trying to 'fix' something else. No commit =
no way back.
Git commit after every small win. Future you
will be grateful.
+

Wireframe loose → build fast → polish later
+
Mistake
Over-designing before building
- I spent days on mockups for Cycle Eats.
Then Claude built it differently anyway. Now
I do rough wireframes and refine as I go.

Mistake
Fighting stuck Claude instead of resetting
- When Claude starts repeating the same bad
fix, prompting harder won't help. Close the
tab. Open a new chat. Give it fresh context.
New chat > 10th retry.
+

Mistake
No plan for what happens after you build it
- "Rent My Mom" went viral but I had no
retention strategy. Now I plan a waitlist
before I write code.

It took me 150+ hours to learn all this
- So I put everything into one guide
vibe-coding 101
for beginners
Cursor

Link in bio
The Vibe Coding Guide
My full workflow from idea → shipped app. Prompting
strategies, tool setup, mistakes to avoid.

Happy vibe coding ✨
and follow for more :)

panel_texts:
CLAUDE AI
5 MIN READ
[Claude can
now think like a
$100M founder
Use these 7
prompts]

Claude
1. The market breakdown system
"Analyze the market for [YOUR NICHE]. Use only
specific, data-backed insights. No generic statements.
God mode genius response that scales with a unique
value proposition only.
Deliver exactly four structured sections:
1. Market sizing: TAM, SAM, and SOM with estimated
dollar values and your assumptions
2. Top 5 demand trends: each as a one-line
headline + two-sentence explanation
3. Top 5 underserved opportunities: specific gaps,
not broad categories
4. Follow the money: 3-5 areas where VC, PE,
or acquirer capital is actively flowing
Format each section with a bold heading, then
concise bullet points. Total output: under 600 words."
CLAUDE
CODE
traded

Claude
2. The problem prioritization engine
"List the top 10 problems in [YOUR INDUSTRY].
For each problem, score it on three dimensions:
• Urgency (1-10): how painful/time-sensitive it is right
now
• Willingness to pay (1-10): how likely buyers are to
spend money to solve it today
• Growth trajectory: "rising fast," "stable," or "declining"
Also add a Complaint signal column: yes/no for
whether this problem surfaces frequently in reviews,
forums, or sales calls.
Output as a table with these exact columns:
| # | Problem | Urgency | WTP | Trend | Complaint
signal | Why it ranks here |
Sort by combined Urgency + WTP score, highest first."
traded

Claude
3. The offer creation framework
"Create a high-converting offer for: [YOUR SPECIFIC
PROBLEM].
Structure the output exactly like a landing page,
with these labeled sections in order:
1. Headline: one bold, benefit-driven statement
2. ICP: who this is for (age, role, situation, pain level)
3. Value proposition: the core transformation in one
sentence
4. Offer components: what's included (deliverables,
bonuses, format)
5. Pricing tiers: name, price, and what changes at
each tier (low / mid / premium)
6. Guarantee: specific risk-reversal language the
customer sees
7. Competitive edge: 3 reasons this beats the
obvious alternatives
Keep each section tight. No filler. Write it as if it will
go directly onto a real landing page."
traded

Claude
4. The distribution domination plan
"Act as a senior growth strategist. Build a realistic 30-
day distribution plan for: [YOUR IDEA], including the
target audience, product type, and rough budget.
Deliverables:
1. Top 5 acquisition channels: ranked by cost-
efficiency for this specific audience
2. Content format per channel: one specific format
that works on each (short-form video, cold email
sequence, SEO article)
3. Weekly execution calendar: what happens in weeks
1, 2, 3, and 4 (not day-by-day)
4. Organic vs paid split: recommended % allocation and
rationale
5. Leverage plays: 2-3 tactics that multiply reach
without proportionally more effort (partnerships,
repurposing, virality hooks)
Be specific and realistic. Skip tactics that require a large
team or $50k+ budget unless the budget context
supports it. Output as a numbered system with clear
section headers."
traded

Claude
5. Viral content engine
"Create a viral content strategy for: [YOUR NICHE].
Deliver four components:
1. Hook bank: 10 high-converting hooks (not 20,
prioritize quality). For each, label which emotional trigger
it uses: fear of missing out, social status, curiosity, or
controversy.
2. Content format matrix: a table with these columns:
Format | Platform | Ideal length | Why it spreads |
Example title. Include 6-8 formats across at least 3
platforms.
3. Shareability audit: for each format, answer "What
makes someone forward/repost this?" in one sentence.
4. Repeatable content system: a simple weekly
template showing how many posts, which formats, and
what rotation keeps the audience engaged without
burnout.
Output with bold section headers. Write the hooks
in the voice of the niche, not generic
marketing language."
traded

Claude
6. The competitor weakness map
"Analyze the top 5 competitors in [YOUR NICHE].
For each competitor, provide a structured row covering:
• Name + one-line description of their core offer
• What they do best (their defensible strength)
• Where they are weak (product gaps, poor reviews,
underserved use cases)
• Which audience they ignore or underserve
Then, based on the patterns across all 5:
• Gap analysis: the 2-3 clearest white spaces no
competitor is owning
• Positioning recommendation: one sharp positioning
statement that would differentiate a new entrant
• Go-to-market angle: which ignored audience + which
channel combination represents the fastest path to
traction
Output the competitor breakdown as a table, then the
gap analysis and recommendations as prose."
traded

Claude
7. The scale system
"Give me a plan to scale this business to [TARGET
REVENUE] within [TIMEFRAME]:
Business description: [Describe your business in 3-5
sentences. Include: what you sell, who buys it, current
monthly revenue, team size, and the biggest bottleneck
you're facing right now]
Structure the output as a phased execution roadmap
with these four phases:
Phase 1 – Stabilize (Month 1-2): what to systematize and
document before scaling
Phase 2 – Automate (Month 3-4): top 3 processes to
automate, with specific tool recommendations
Phase 3 – Delegate (Month 5-8): what to hire for first, in
order, with rough cost per role
Phase 4 – Scale (Month 9-12): the growth lever (channel,
product, or partnership) that unlocks
the next revenue tier...
traded

Claude
7. The scale system
... Also include:
Top 3 bottlenecks that will appear at each phase
transition
• One leading metric to track per phase (not vanity
metrics)
• Output as a structured roadmap with phase
headers, not a generic list."
traded

5. Leverage plays: 2-3 tactics that multiply reach
without proportionally more effort (partnerships,
repurposing, virality hooks)
Be specific and realistic. Skip tactics that require a large
team or $50k+ budget unless the budget context
supports it. Output as a numbered system with clear
section headers."
traded

Panel 6: Claude
5. Viral content engine
"Create a viral content strategy for: [YOUR NICHE].
Deliver four components:
1. Hook bank: 10 high-converting hooks (not 20,
prioritize quality). For each, label which emotional trigger
it uses: fear of missing out, social status, curiosity, or
controversy.
2. Content format matrix: a table with these columns:
Format | Platform | Ideal length | Why it spreads |
Example title. Include 6-8 formats across at least 3
platforms.
3. Shareability audit: for each format, answer "What
makes someone forward/repost this?" in one sentence.
4. Repeatable content system: a simple weekly
template showing how many posts, which formats, and
what rotation keeps the audience engaged without
burnout.
Output with bold section headers. Write the hooks
in the voice of the niche, not generic
marketing language."
traded

Panel 7: Claude
6. The competitor weakness map
"Analyze the top 5 competitors in [YOUR NICHE].
For each competitor, provide a structured row covering:
• Name + one-line description of their core offer
• What they do best (their defensible strength)
• Where they are weak (product gaps, poor reviews,
underserved use cases)
• Which audience they ignore or underserve
Then, based on the patterns across all 5:
• Gap analysis: the 2-3 clearest white spaces no
competitor is owning
• Positioning recommendation: one sharp positioning
statement that would differentiate a new entrant
• Go-to-market angle: which ignored audience + which
channel combination represents the fastest path to
traction
Output the competitor breakdown as a table, then the
gap analysis and recommendations as prose."
traded

7. The scale system
"Give me a plan to scale this business to [TARGET
REVENUE] within [TIMEFRAME]:
Business description: [Describe your business in 3-5
sentences. Include: what you sell, who buys it, current
monthly revenue, team size, and the biggest bottleneck
you're facing right now]
Structure the output as a phased execution roadmap
with these four phases:
Phase 1 – Stabilize (Month 1-2): what to systematize and
document before scaling
Phase 2 – Automate (Month 3-4): top 3 processes to
automate, with specific tool recommendations
Phase 3 – Delegate (Month 5-8): what to hire for first, in
order, with rough cost per role
Phase 4 – Scale (Month 9-12): the growth lever (channel,
product, or partnership) that unlocks
the next revenue tier...

Top 3 bottlenecks that will appear at each phase
transition
• One leading metric to track per phase (not vanity
metrics)
• Output as a structured roadmap with phase
headers, not a generic list."

slideshows.description: Most developers set up Claude Code wrong from day one. Here's the exact file system you can literally steal: 👇 ☑ Step 1: The 4 Core Files → CLAUDE. md loads your core rules every session. → CLAUDE.local. md holds overrides that never reach git. → AGENTS. md defines who does what, and handoffs. → mcp. JSON connects Claude to 200+ external tools. ☑ Step 2: Rules and Commands → rules/. md stores one focused rule per topic. → commands/. md turns files into custom slash commands. → Type / in chat to see commands. ☑ Step 3: Skills and Agents → skills/. md auto-triggers based on detected task context. → Each skill is one focused, single-purpose directory. → agents/. md runs isolated, with its own tools. ☑ Step 4: Hooks and Memory → hooks/. sh enforce rules through a deterministic shell. → PreToolUse blocks actions before they ever run. → memory/. md persists the project context across sessions. ☑ Step 5: Workflows → workflows/ .md defines repeatable blueprints for builds, reviews. → Claude follows blueprints using skills, agents, and hooks. #claudecode #claudeprojects #claudeskills #claudeprompt #ai  → One workflow file replaces ten repeated prompts.

CLAUDE.md Loaded every single session.
Project overview, tech stack, coding conventions, architecture notes, hard rules, and
safety boundaries. Under 200 lines-every line earns its space.
CLAUDE.local.md Personal overrides. Never committed.
Your machine-specific paths, personal preferences, and experimental rules.
Gitignored. Stacks on top of CLAUDE.md - never replaces it.
AGENTS.md The team roster. Who does what.
Defines every subagent's role, capabilities, and handoff protocol. Claude reads this
before delegating. Prevents overlap. Keeps multi-agent sessions coordinated.
mcp.json MCP server integrations. Shared via git.
Connects Claude to GitHub, Notion, Slack, Gmail, PostgreSQL, Jira, and 200+ tools
settings.json Permissions, tools, and hooks config.
Defines what Claude can read, write, and execute. Allow and deny lists. Hook events
wired here. Committed to git-personal overrides go in settings.local.json.
rules/md-Modular rule files. Loaded on demand.
Each .md is a focused rule module code style, API conventions, testing standards, PR
format. Keeps CLAUDE.md lean by externalizing detail that only loads when relevant.
commands/*.md Custom slash commands for your project.
Each.md becomes a/project.command-name. Supports SARGUMENTS for user input.
Perfect for PR reviews, deploys, and scaffolding. Type / in chat to see all commands.
skills/<name>/SKILL.md-Auto-triggered by task context.
Not a single file-a directory per skill. The description field is the routing rule. Loads
only when Claude recognizes the task. One job per Skill. Keeps context lightweight.
agents/md-Specialized subagents with isolated context.
Own system prompt, own tools, own permissions. Runs in a separate context
window-research without polluting main session. Invoke with @agent-name.
hooks/sh Event-driven scripts. 100% enforcement.
Make sure Claude does something deterministically via shell commands - not LLM
interpretation. PreToolUse blocks. PostTooluse reacts. Exit 0 allow. Exit 2 block
memory/.md-Persistent ent memory across all sessions.
Project context, architectural decisions, and progress logs Claude reads between
sessions. Compensates for context loss in long projects. Commit to git-the
whole team benefits.
workflows/*.md-Multi-step task blueprints.
Each .md defines a repeatable workflow feature build, bug fix, code review
cycle. Claude follows the blueprint step by step. Combines Skills, Subagents, and
Hooks in sequence.

Don't build an autonomous coding agent on day one. Build one loop that reliably solves one problem, then improve it over time.

panel_texts:
Claude Hacks I Wish
I Knew Before
• Use the Desktop app, not the browser.
• Use Cowork, not the chatbot.
• The longer the chat, the worse it gets.
• Clear your chats. Long ones cost you.
• Edit your messy files in Obsidian (it's free).
• "Go beyond the basics" on creative work.
• A token is one word & every word costs you money.
• Don't give Claude steps. Give it the goal.
• Don't paste logins, passwords, or keys. Ever.
• Skills fire themselves. Just /command.
• It sounds sure even when it's wrong.
• Don't give Claude steps. Give it the goal.
• The about-me file is everything.
• Use Research mode. Nobody knows it's there.
• Give it five very different versions. Pick one.
• Projects now remember between sessions.
• Upload 30 docs. Ask what's working.
• The first draft is yours to fix, not ship.
• Claude is for coding & knowledge work. Not health.
• AskUser Question is the best feature nobody uses.
• Make it audit its own answer before you trust it.
• Outsource the thinking, never the understanding.
• Hand it the hardest task you've got. That's where it wins.
• Stop prompting like before. Forget your prompt library.
• Don't trust agreement. Claude is a sycophant.

from Ruben Hassid, on "How to AI"

slideshows.description: Run Claude Code completely free using Ollama and open source models. No API key. No monthly bill. Here’s the exact 4-step setup: Step 1 — Check your hardware. You need at least 16GB RAM, 20GB free for the model, and either 32GB Apple Silicon or 16–24GB NVIDIA VRAM. Step 2 — Install Ollama. One curl command and it’s running locally on your machine. Step 3 — Pull a coding model. GLM-4.7-Flash is 4.7GB and handles code tasks well. Step 4 — Install Claude Code and point it at Ollama. Claude Code is now running on a fully local, free model. This works because Claude Code supports custom model endpoints — Ollama exposes a local API that Claude Code can talk to. No Anthropic account needed after setup. . . #claude #claudecode #claudeskills #claudeai #ollama

slideshows.description: Everyone's talking about AI agents and autonomous workflows. But most people are still copy-pasting between ChatGPT and Google Docs like it's 2023. This setup connects three tools that weren't designed to work together, and turns them into something that keeps getting better without you doing extra work. Claude Code runs the show. NotebookLM does the expensive processing on Google's dime. Obsidian stores everything so nothing gets lost. And the whole thing learns your style over time. The guy who built this said it takes under 30 minutes to set up. After a month of use, the difference is real. After a year with hundreds of documents? He called it a "huge lasting effect." I think the biggest insight here isn't even the tools. It's that most people never build systems around their AI usage. They just have conversations that disappear. This is the opposite of that. What's your current setup for keeping AI context between sessions? Genuinely curious because most solutions I've seen are either way too simple or way too complicated. #ClaudeCode #NotebookLM #Obsidian #AIWorkflow #AITools

itsmariahbrunner
Mariah Brunner | Al with Mariah
COMMANDS
01. /SCHEDULE
Set tasks to run on repeat. Daily, weekly, whenever.
02. TYPE "/"
Pulls up every Skill installed. Fastest way to find what Cowork can do.
03. CUSTOMIZE → CONNECTORS
Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Slack. Half of Cowork won't work without these.
04. WORKING FOLDER
Set my working folder to /Documents/Projects." Scopes every file action.
05. MEMORY
Cowork remembers your preferences per project.
Set once, works forever.
03

itsmariahbrunner

Queue Cowork tasks from your phone.
Your desktop runs them when you're back.

"Rename everything in /Downloads using date_description_type."
10. SMART DEDUPLICATION
"Find all duplicates across /Documents. Show me before deleting."
04

"Find the [project] thread. Tell me what was decided, what's open,
who's doing what."

"Find everything about [project] across Drive, Slack, Gmail.

slideshows.description: Anthropic quietly pushed Sonnet 5 as the new default for Free and Pro plans as of today June 30 2026. Here is what actually changed: What Sonnet 5 is: Sonnet 5 sits between Haiku and Opus in the Claude model family. It is the middle tier faster than Opus, more capable than Haiku. But this version is different from every Sonnet before it. Anthropic is calling it the most agentic Sonnet ever built. What agentic means in plain English: Previous Sonnet models would start a complex task and stall halfway. They would stop and ask you what to do next. Sonnet 5 finishes the job. It makes plans. It uses tools like browsers and terminals. It checks its own output without being asked. It runs from start to finish without needing you in the middle. One engineer at Zapier said they gave Sonnet 5 a two-part job update Salesforce account tiers and send a launch announcement to enterprise contacts. It finished end to end. That task used to stall halfway through. The performance numbers: Sonnet 5 scores 63.2% on agentic coding benchmarks. Opus 4.8 scores 69.2%. The gap between the middle model and the top model has never been this small. On knowledge work benchmarks Sonnet 5 actually slightly outperforms Opus 4.8. You now get near-Opus performance at Sonnet pricing. The pricing: Through August 31 2026  $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. After August 31 $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens. That makes Sonnet 5 cheaper than Opus 4.8, cheaper than OpenAI’s GPT-5.5, and cheaper than Google’s Gemini 3.1 Pro. The safety improvements: Sonnet 5 hallucinates less than Sonnet 4.6. It is less sycophantic meaning it agrees with you less and pushes back more when you are wrong. It refuses malicious requests more consistently. It is harder to manipulate through prompt injection attacks. Claude Code users: Sonnet 5 is now the default model in Claude Code as well. It comes with a native 1 million token context window meaning it can hold an entire large codebase in its working memory at once. What this means for you: If you are on a Free plan your Claude just got significantly more capable today at no extra cost. If you are on a Pro plan same thing. If you have been waiting to try Claude because you thought it was too expensive today is the day. The most capable mid-tier model Anthropic has ever built is now the default on the free plan. The gap between free and paid AI is closing faster than anyone expected. Save this. Share it with everyone who uses Claude. 👇🔥 #ClaudeAI #ClaudeSonnet5 #TheClaudeFiles #Anthropic #AINews

Mistakes 99% of beginners do
when vibecoding:

1. Bad Prompting
Bad prompt: build me a calorie
tracking app that analyzes food
pictures
Good prompt: create a react native
expo app to analyze and keep track
of my calories with OCR and image
recognition using the openAl api
as detailed in the prd.md doc. Draw up
a plan first and ask me any
clarifying questions

2. Context Overload
Asking for too many edits across
files in the same chat will make the
Al agent hallucinate and start
editing random files.
Always keep context limited, and
isolate individual implementations
to dedicated chats/agents

3. No Clear PRD Docs
You must have a detailed, clear,
and complete prd doc in markdown
format that outlines the tech stack,
user flow, frontend & backend
architecture, API usage, important
points, etc...
This will make sure that your ai
agents always understand the
general goal of the project.
You ca have more individual md
docs to detail steps of
implementation more in depth

YOU'RE VIBE CODING WRONG.
7 mistakes that kill your project —
and exactly how to fix each one
SWIPE TO FIX IT →
panel_texts:
AI INGEST
VIBE CODERS, LISTEN UP
YOU'RE VIBE
CODING
WRONG.
7 mistakes that kill your project —
and exactly how to fix each one
SWIPE TO FIX IT →

MISTAKE 01 / 07
MOST COMMON
JUST WINGING IT
Typing "build me an app" with no plan.
Claude starts coding immediately — then
you spend hours fixing a wrong
foundation. It's always faster to plan first.
THE FIX
USE PLAN MODE FIRST
"Enter Plan Mode. Design the full
architecture before writing any code."

MISTAKE 02 / 07
KILLS CONSISTENCY
NO MEMORY FILE
Every new session, Claude forgets your
stack, your style, your rules. You repeat
yourself every single time — wasting
tokens and getting inconsistent output.
THE FIX
CREATE CLAUDE.MD
Add your stack, colours, rules. Claude
reads it automatically every session.

MISTAKE 03 / 07
WASTES HOURS
CODING BLIND
Claude can't see what it built. So when
something breaks, you become its eyes —
describing errors, copying console output,
going in circles for hours.
THE FIX
INSTALL CLAUDE IN CHROME
Claude sees your site live and fixes
visual bugs itself. No describing
needed.

MISTAKE 04 / 07
CAUSES CHAOS
GIANT PROMPTS
Asking Claude to build 10 features in one
prompt. It tries to do everything at once,
breaks half of it, and you can't tell which
change caused which bug.
THE FIX
ONE FEATURE AT A TIME
Build → test → approve → next feature.
Use a task list in CLAUDE.md.

MISTAKE 05 / 07
CLASSIC TRAP
TRUSTING BLINDLY
Accepting Claude's output without testing
it. Looks fine until production — then
everything breaks and you can't trace
which change caused it.
THE FIX
MAKE CLAUDE SELF-VERIFY
"Prove to me this works. Don't finish
until it does."

MISTAKE 06 / 07
CODE SPAGHETTI
ENDLESS PATCHES
Patching broken code over and over. The
fixes pile up, the code gets messier, and
eventually Claude can't even understand
what it built anymore.
THE FIX
USE THE RESET PROMPT
"Knowing what you know now — scrap
this and implement the elegant
solution."

MISTAKE 07 / 07
COSTS YOU MONEY
USING ONE MODEL
Using Opus for everything burns through
your credits fast. Most coding tasks don't
need the most expensive model — and
Sonnet is often faster anyway.
THE FIX
MATCH MODEL TO TASK
Haiku → quick edits. Sonnet → most
builds. Opus → complex architecture
only.
